title: Octopus Ragù with Bottarga
summary: A slow octopus ragù with tomatoes, olives and capers, tossed with paccheri and finished off the heat with lemon and bottarga.

items.note: or mezzi paccheri, rigatoni or thick spaghetti

steps.heading: Cook the octopus
steps.text: Put the octopus in a large, heavy pot with the wine, the vinegar, and the bay leaf and peppercorns, if using. Cover tightly with a lid.
Cook over a low heat for {timer:60-90|octopus}. The octopus releases its own liquid, which makes a concentrated broth.
Check it is tender: a fork should go easily into the thickest part of a tentacle. Lift the octopus out, keep the cooking liquid, and cut the octopus into 2-3 cm pieces.

steps.heading: Build the ragù
steps.text: Heat the olive oil in a large pan or casserole over a medium-low heat. Add the onion and cook it slowly for {timer:8-10}, until soft and sweet.
Add the garlic and cook for {timer:1}. Add the anchovies, if using, and let them melt.
Add the octopus and cook for {timer:5}. Pour in the wine and let it reduce for {timer:2-3}.
Add the tomatoes, the olives, the capers and the octopus cooking liquid.
Simmer gently, partly covered, for {timer:1.5-2h|ragù}, until the sauce is thick and glossy and clings to the octopus.

steps.heading: Lemon bottarga
steps.text: Put the olive oil for the lemon bottarga in a small bowl. Add the bottarga, the lemon zest, the parsley and the pepper, if using, and mix into a thick paste. Let it sit for {timer:10-15} before it goes into the pasta.

steps.heading: The pasta
steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil and cook the pasta until 2 minutes before al dente. Keep some of the pasta water.
Add the pasta straight to the ragù and toss for {timer:1-2}, adding pasta water until it is silky.

steps.heading: Finish
steps.text: Turn off the heat. Add the lemon bottarga and toss well, with a splash of pasta water if it looks dry.

tips: Never fry or boil the bottarga: heat dulls its aroma, which is the whole point. It goes in at the end, off the heat, like a seasoning.
Add no salt at all. Between the octopus, capers, olives, anchovies and bottarga there is plenty, which is also why the anchovies are kept to a minimum.
Paccheri or mezzi paccheri are the best choice: the thick tubes hold the octopus ragù and the bottarga beautifully.
If the ragù gets too thick as it simmers, add a little more of the octopus cooking liquid.
As a guide, 1 large onion is about 150-180 g, and 2 tbsp of grated bottarga about 25-30 g.
Crushed tomatoes work instead of the cherry tomatoes: use a little less by weight, about 350 g for every 400 g.
